newsitem.title: USA: GM November U.S. vehicle sales fall 12 percent.
newsitem.headline: GM November U.S. vehicle sales fall 12 percent.

text.p: Sales of General Motors Corp.'s car and trucks in November, hurt by work stoppages in the United States and Canada, fell nearly 12 percent from a year ago, the automaker said Tuesday.
GM said it sold a total of 336,815 vehicles in the U.S. market last month as car sales plunged 22.5 percent to 179,150 while total truck light sales rose to 157,665, an increase of 4.2 percent.

The automaker said November sales of its full-size pickup trucks and sport/utility vehicles, as well as Chevrolet Lumina, Monte Carlo, Cavalier and Cadillac Deville car lines, were held back by lost production due to United Auto Worker and Canadian Auto Worker strikes in October and early November.
Chevrolet, GM's largest division, had November sales of 169,110, a more than 13 percent drop from 194,973 a year ago. Pontiac sales fell 8.5 percent to 40,550.
So far this year, GM's total sales were 4,447,147, a decline of 1.7 percent from the first 11 months of 1995.

Ronald Zarrella, GM's top marketing executive, noted that sales of the new Pontiac Grand Prix were up 46 percent in November, a sign that buyers like the redesigned vehicles GM is introducing over the next several months.
"This strong consumer acceptance of our new products will increase in the months ahead as we continue to roll out more of our new 1997 models," he said in a statement.

However, GM's numbers, which came one day after Chrysler Corp. reported a 1.4 percent increase in November sales, confirmed analyst projections that November will be a weak month for Detroit's Big Three.

That was not the case with two Japanese automakers, Toyota Motor Corp. and Honda Motor Co. Ltd. Spurred by strong sales of its new Camry sedan, Toyota had total November sales of 99,241, a 19.6 percent increase.

"Consumer confidence and spending have proven surprisingly resilient in the fourth quarter, driving industry sales far beyond expectations," Yale Gieszl, executive vice president of Toyota Motor Sales USA Inc., said in a statement.
Toyota sold 31,644 Camry's last month, a 31 percent increase and its best-ever November performance. Total sport/utility sales were 16,268, up more than 100 percent from a year ago.

Toyota said its new 4Runner had sales of 9,040, a record for November and an increase of 35.3 percent. The RAV4 mini sport/utility continues to exceed sales expectations, with November sales of 5,321.
Honda sales rose nearly 16 percent to 70,534, riding the strength of the company's Accord, which had a 41 percent jump in sales to 32,719.
"Consumers recognise the value of our Honda Accord," said Dick Colliver, Honda Division senior vice president of sales.
While total car sales for Honda rose 16.8 percent to 68,136, Honda's light truck sales fell 6 percent to 2,398.
Ford Motor Corp. will report its November sales on Wednesday.
